summary.title: HiFi-UMI: Learning Deployable Manipulation Policies from High-Fidelity UMI Data Alone

setting_and_object.category: System & Dataset (hardware–software data-production pipeline plus released corpus)

details: Robot-free handheld (UMI-style) capture scales cheaply but is assumed usable only for pre-training, with a real-robot teleoperation 'anchor' still required for post-training; the paper argues the true limitation is data fidelity, not the robot-free setting.

HiFi-UMI: a portable, infrastructure-free handheld bimanual capture device co-designed for fidelity — head-mounted offline stereo-inertial SLAM with per-hand fiducial cubes (giving natively measured inter-gripper relative pose), a single shared GPIO hardware trigger for microsecond cross-sensor sync, two non-parallel fisheye cameras per hand (~200° coverage), and a full-palm glove gripper.

An automated data flywheel (reconstruct → simulation replay validation → AI annotation → human verification → balanced export) that turns raw captures into robot-executable, curated episodes; plus the released HiFi-UMI-2K corpus.
Central claim tested: 'zero-robot post-training' — post-training solely on this robot-free data yields policies deployable on a real robot without any teleoperated data.
Full corpus: 20,000+ hours, 4.32M+ episodes, 480+ scenes, six synchronized camera views per episode.
Released HiFi-UMI-2K: 2,000 hours, 482,100+ episodes, 110+ scenes, CC BY 4.0, faces masked.

Measured fidelity: ~3 mm local end-effector error over ~2 m workspace vs base-station ground truth, <40 µs cross-sensor offset, <1 dropped frame per 270,000, gripper angle error <0.1°; 98% SLAM reconstruction × 98% replay validation ≈ 96% usable yield.
Deliberately forgoes global loop closure (scene is non-static during manipulation); local sliding-window consistency bounds drift to centimeters globally while preserving millimeter local accuracy.

Three backbones: StarVLA-QwenPI (Qwen3-VL-4B + flow-matching DiT action head, trained by the authors), OpenPI-π0.5 (from pi05_base), and LingBot-VA (world-action model decoding actions from predicted future video latents, from lingbot-va-base).
Seven conditions: HiFi-UMI vs teleoperation post-training per backbone (C1–C6), plus HiFi-UMI pre-training → HiFi-UMI post-training on StarVLA-QwenPI (C7).

Shared physical action semantics across backbones: chunk-anchored relative SE(3) increments (translation in anchor EE frame, Rotation6D) plus absolute gripper, 10 channels per arm; only the four wrist views feed the policy (head stereo used solely for reconstruction).
Pre-training: 4,000 hours of multi-task UMI data, 180k steps (one pass), global batch 2,048, AdamW; post-training 50k steps at batch 512 (VLA) / 3,500 steps at batch 32 (LingBot-VA).
Bimanual platform with two 7-DoF Tianji Marvin M6 force-controlled arms carrying the same gripper and four wrist cameras as the capture rig; IK at 125 Hz, EtherCAT at 1 kHz.
Four tasks: Stain Wiping, Shirt Folding, Remote Insertion, Produce Sorting; 40 rollouts per task–policy pair, 960 rollouts total across six data-source conditions.

Frozen benchmark before evaluation (task definitions, checkpoints, initial-condition bank, timeouts, safety rules), separate policy operator and scene operator, randomized policy order, recorded termination reasons; binary success with 2 s stability requirement.
Per task: 3,200 UMI trajectories (~10–20 h) collected by multiple operators across sites, versus ~300 teleoperation trajectories (~3–7 h) collected on the target robot in the evaluation scene.

No HiFi-UMI trajectory is collected in the evaluation scene, so the UMI condition faces scene-level distribution shift while teleoperation is in-domain; comparison is pipeline-level, not sample-matched.
Post-training data scaling on Remote Insertion with OpenPI-π0.5 at 400/800/1,600/3,200/6,400 episodes.
Initialization ablation on StarVLA-QwenPI (Qwen3-VL + scratch action head vs UMI-pretrained) at matched 3,200 episodes and in the low-data regime.
Held-out action-error scaling fits during pre-training and an OOD set of ten separately collected unseen tasks.
Oracle 'ground-truth-video' diagnostic for LingBot-VA comparing Real→Real, UMI→Real, UMI→UMI pose decoding against random-action references, with bootstrap CIs over source episodes.

key_findings.finding: Post-training solely on high-fidelity robot-free HiFi-UMI data matches in-domain real-robot teleoperation across three backbones, with no consistent direction of difference.
key_findings.evidence: Aggregate success-rate differences (UMI minus teleop) of -2.5 pp on StarVLA-QwenPI (51.3% vs 53.8%), +3.1 pp on OpenPI-π0.5 (77.5% vs 74.4%), and -0.6 pp on LingBot-VA (56.9% vs 57.5%), over 960 rollouts under a pre-frozen benchmark, despite the teleop data being collected in the evaluation scene and no UMI trajectory being; OpenPI-π0.5 reaches 85% on Remote Insertion.

key_findings.finding: Head-mounted offline stereo-inertial SLAM plus a shared GPIO trigger deliver teleoperation-grade capture fidelity without any external tracking infrastructure.
key_findings.evidence: Measured ~3 mm local end-effector error over ~2 m of head-trajectory length (matching base-station-dependent systems such as FastUMI Pro), <40 µs cross-sensor timing offset (vs millisecond software alignment in prior systems), <0.1° gripper-angle error, and a 96% cumulative usable-data yield from two serial 98% gates (reconstruction, simulation replay).

key_findings.finding: Large-scale robot-free pre-training improves both post-training data efficiency and the attainable deployment ceiling.
key_findings.evidence: On StarVLA-QwenPI, 4,000 hours of UMI pre-training raises aggregate real-robot success by 18.1 pp at matched 3,200 post-training episodes, and on Remote Insertion surpasses the Qwen-VL-initialized 3,200-episode baseline with only 800 episodes (80% at 1,600); held-out action error falls 61% over one pass with power-law exponent alpha=0.268 (R^2=0.993).

key_findings.finding: Out-of-distribution transfer is governed more by coverage of interaction dynamics in the pre-training mixture than by whether test objects were seen.
key_findings.evidence: Mean action error on ten unseen tasks drops 41% (aggregate power-law exponent 0.095), but improvement rates order as utensil/tableware > granular transfer > cloth folding, mirroring the mixture composition where object/receptacle placement is over one third of frames while textile folding is under one percent.

key_findings.finding: UMI-only post-training saturates in the low-data regime, and its action decoder transfers across observation domains with minimal degradation.
key_findings.evidence: Remote Insertion success rises 37.5%→65%→70%→85% for 400/800/1,600/3,200 episodes then plateaus (82.5% at 6,400); under ground-truth-video conditioning the UMI-post-trained LingBot-VA decoder gives 24.33 mm XYZ RMSE and 0.65° SO(3) error on held-out real-robot observations vs 21.13 mm / 0.88° on held-out UMI observations and 21.64 mm / 0.46° for the teleop-trained reference (random actions: ~118 mm / 126°).
